name: Dandruff
description: Dandruff is a common scalp condition characterized by the excessive production of skin cells on the scalp, leading to flaky white or gray scales and flakes that can be seen in the hair or on clothes. It can also cause itching.
symptoms: Flaking of the scalp, visible as white or gray scales
Redness and inflammation on the scalp
Greasy residue on hair and shoulders
risk_factors: Certain Medical Conditions (such as HIV/AIDS, Parkinson's Disease)

daily_routine.purpose: Helps remove excess oil and flakes, preventing buildup.

daily_routine.step: Apply a leave-in treatment or conditioner after shampooing
daily_routine.purpose: Provides nourishment to the scalp and hair, helping to reduce flakiness.

natural_remedies: Applying Olive Oil or Coconut Oil to the Scalp
Rinsing with Apple Cider Vinegar Solution
lifestyle_tips: Maintain a Healthy Diet Rich in Omega-3 Fatty Acids and Antioxidants
Manage Stress Through Exercise, Meditation, or Therapy
Avoid Harsh Chemicals and Irritants in Hair Care Products
common_myths: Dandruff is caused by poor hygiene.
Shampooing more often will get rid of dandruff.
Only people with oily scalps can have dandruff.
when_to_consult_doctor: If over-the-counter treatments do not improve symptoms, if there are signs of infection (redness, pain, pus), or if the condition significantly affects daily life.
prevention: Regularly Cleansing the Scalp to Prevent Buildup

severity_levels.mild: Minimal flaking, no significant discomfort or changes in appearance. Symptoms may be manageable with over-the-counter products.
severity_levels.moderate: Moderate scaling and itching, visible flakes on clothing. May require stronger shampoos or additional home care measures.
severity_levels.severe: Severe scaling, intense itching, and redness. Requires professional treatment to manage symptoms.

expert_tips: Patch Test New Products Before Full Application
Consult a Dermatologist for Persistent Cases
Stay Hydrated and Maintain Overall Skin Health
